robot.name: Rainbow Robotics RB-Y1
robot.generation: first-generation RB-Y1 wheeled bimanual mobile manipulator
robot.status_notes: Pre-orders began May 8, 2024; deliveries scheduled to start October 2024. MERA Robotics directory lists status as Shipping as of comparison date. No public deployment or customer report found.
intended_use_cases: research platform for AI and manipulation learning

height.original_value: 600 x 690 x 1,400mm (W x D x H)
height.notes: Height 1,400 mm = 140 cm. Overall dimensions 600 x 690 x 1,400 mm.

weight.original_value: Upper body: 38kg (Arm 11kg x 2, Torso 16kg) Lower body: 42kg Mobile: 51kg Total: 131kg
weight.notes: Configuration A total 131 kg; Configuration M total 170 kg (Mobile 90 kg).

payload.notes: Per-arm payload from official page. MERA Robotics directory lists 20 kg total, conflicting with official spec.

runtime.notes: Runtime not published. Battery capacity provided but no runtime estimate found.

battery.notes: Configuration A has 1,250 Wh; Configuration M has 2,500 Wh.

walking_speed.notes: Official driving speed. Industrial Automation Magazine reports 2.5m/s, conflict noted.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: Spec table: total 20 DOF (Configuration A) or 26 DOF (Configuration M). Breakdown: Wheel A 1 DOF x2, Wheel M 1 DOF x4, Leg 6, Arm 7 x2, Head 2. Page text also states 24 DOF overall system configuration; inconsistency noted.

hands.description: Optional gripper available (no detailed specs on official product page). Force/torque sensors on both arms are built into V1.2 configuration.

items: Vision sensor bracket provided (camera not included)

compute.description: Dual-PC architecture: real-time Robot PC and User PC with ROS 2 and SDK.

actuators.description: Actuator technology verified by cooperative robots; joint brake structure; joint speeds and ranges listed in spec table.

availability.notes: Pre-order price $80,000 research, $120,000 commercial (VAT excluded) announced May 2024; delivery scheduled starting October 2024.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: Official specs list two 7-DoF arms, per-arm payload 3 kg, repeatability ±0.05 mm, and force/torque sensors on both arms (V1.2). Media article references performance videos including water pouring and cup stacking, but videos not directly reviewed.
caveats: No direct video analysis; demo details from media titles only.
Per-arm payload is 3 kg, not 20 kg as some directories state.
Gripper specifications not detailed on official page.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: PR Newswire states LiDAR system is adopted for autonomous movement. No evidence of autonomous manipulation or end-to-end task execution. Teleoperation video title exists (source 9), but no autonomy demonstration reviewed.
caveats: Only autonomous movement claimed; no autonomous task execution evidence.
No intervention logs or independent autonomy validation.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Wheeled base with driving speed 1.5 m/s (official). Spec table shows leg 6 DOF and full-body control architecture. Industrial Automation Magazine reports 2.5 m/s and video demo 'Dynamic driving' exists (source 3).
caveats: Wheeled base, not biped; mobility limited to flat surfaces.
Speed conflict between official (1.5 m/s) and media (2.5 m/s).
Video not directly reviewed.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Official page lists LiDAR, optional high-performance 3D recognition sensor, and force/torque sensors. No perception benchmarks or scene understanding demonstrations found.
caveats: Sensors are listed but performance not demonstrated.
No third-party perception evaluation.

human_interaction.summary: Teleoperation via leader arm or VR device is supported (source 1, 5). Product page mentions suitability for human-robot interaction research. No demonstrated social or conversational interaction.
caveats: No evidence of autonomous interaction.
Teleoperation interface is for human control, not autonomous social behavior.

endurance_reliability.summary: Product page claims actuator technology verified by cooperative robots and joint brake structure for reliable long experiments. No endurance test data or customer reliability reports found.
caveats: No uptime, MTBF, or long-duration test evidence.
Company claim only.

human_environment_fit.summary: Wheeled base, height 140 cm, weight 131 kg (Configuration A), aluminum exterior, safety functions listed (current limits, position errors). Designed for industrial/research environments, not home use.
caveats: Wheeled base cannot handle stairs or rough terrain.
Heavy at 131 kg; no safety certification found.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: Pre-orders announced with delivery schedule, but no named customers or deployed units found. MERA Robotics directory lists status as Shipping, but no commercial deployment evidence.
caveats: Pre-orders are not deployment proof.
No customer press releases or independent reports of RB-Y1 in use.

accessibility_value.summary: Official pre-order price: $80,000 (research) and $120,000 (commercial) VAT excluded, with deliveries starting October 2024. Product is purchasable via contact.
caveats: Price from May 2024 announcement; may have changed.
No current stock or subsequent pricing confirmed.

evidence_items.title: RB-Y1 official product page specifications
evidence_items.claim: Official product page lists dimensions 600x690x1400mm, per-arm payload 3kg, arm repeatability ±0.05mm, driving speed 1.5m/s, and configurations A (20 DOF, 131kg, 1,250Wh) and M (26 DOF, 170kg, 2,500Wh).
evidence_items.notes: Official spec page; values not independently measured.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Defines size, payload, speed, DoF and battery for comparison.
evidence_items.source_location: Rainbow Robotics RB-Y1 product page, specification table

evidence_items.title: Pre-order pricing and delivery
evidence_items.claim: Rainbow Robotics began pre-orders for RB-Y1 on May 8, 2024; research platform $80,000 and commercial platform $120,000 (VAT excluded), with deliveries starting October 2024.
evidence_items.notes: Official pre-order announcement via PR Newswire.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: During the pre-order period, the research platform is sold for $80,000 USD and the commercial platform is sold for $120,000 USD (VAT excluded).
evidence_items.verification_notes: Official press release; no later pricing updates found.

evidence_items.title: LiDAR autonomous movement claim
evidence_items.claim: Rainbow Robotics states the LiDAR system is adopted for autonomous movement.
evidence_items.notes: Company claim; no autonomous navigation demo reviewed.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The LiDAR system is adopted for autonomous movement, and a high-performance 3D recognition sensor and master ARM are provided as options to increase usability.

evidence_items.title: Performance video links
evidence_items.claim: Industrial Automation Magazine lists performance videos for dynamic driving, water pouring, and cup stacking on Rainbow Robotics YouTube.
evidence_items.notes: Media article with video links; videos not directly reviewed.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Indicates demonstrated manipulation and mobility, but unverified.
evidence_items.source_location: Reference section of Industrial Automation India article
evidence_items.verification_notes: Article titles mention demos; no transcript or content review.

evidence_items.title: Driving speed conflict
evidence_items.claim: Industrial Automation Magazine reports driving operation speed 2.5m/s, conflicting with official 1.5m/s.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The driving operation speed is 2.5m/s, and various types of high-speed turning and sudden acceleration are possible using 20-axis full-body control.
evidence_items.source_location: Industrial Automation India article, second paragraph
evidence_items.verification_notes: Single media report; not confirmed by company.

evidence_items.title: Directory payload conflict
evidence_items.claim: MERA Robotics directory lists RB-Y1 payload as 20 kg and says no official price, while official sources state 3 kg per arm and pre-order price $80,000.
evidence_items.notes: Directory page may have incorrect data; conflict documented.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Rainbow Robotics RB-Y1 has a higher payload (20 kg vs 2 kg).
evidence_items.source_location: MERA Robotics comparison page, first summary line

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: RB-Y1 is a purchasable wheeled bimanual mobile manipulator with strong official specs (two 7-DOF arms, ±0.05 mm repeatability, 20/26 DOF, 1.5 m/s) aimed at research and teleoperation. It has pre-order pricing and delivery, but no named deployments, autonomy demos, or verified video evidence beyond titles. Best used for manipulation and teleoperation research claims.
strongest_positive_evidence: Official product page with detailed specs and dual-arm whole-body control architecture.
Pre-order announcement with pricing and delivery schedule.
Media report listing performance videos including water pouring and cup stacking (videos not reviewed).
Force/torque sensors and LiDAR with optional 3D sensor.
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No video transcript or content review; only titles.
No named customers or deployment metrics.
No autonomy demonstration beyond autonomous movement claim.
No runtime or endurance test data.
conflicting_claims: Driving speed 1.5 m/s (official) vs 2.5 m/s (Industrial Automation Magazine).
Payload 3 kg per arm (official) vs 20 kg total (MERA Robotics directory).
Total DOF 20/26 (spec table) vs 24 in page text.
do_not_overclaim: Do not credit specific manipulation capabilities from video titles without content review.
Do not claim autonomous task execution.
Do not treat pre-orders as commercial deployment.
Do not use 20 kg payload; use 3 kg per arm.
Do not infer runtime from battery capacity alone.

currentness.currentness_notes: RB-Y1 is current product as of 2026-10-29; no successor found in reviewed sources.

excluded_claims.reason: MERA Robotics directory lists 20 kg, conflicting with official 3 kg per arm.
Industrial Automation Magazine reports 2.5 m/s, conflicting with official 1.5 m/s.
Product page text says 24 DOF, but spec table clearly lists 20 (A) and 26 (M). Spec table used.
MERA Robotics directory says no official price, but PR Newswire has official pre-order pricing.

excluded_claims.claim: Specific capabilities from video titles (e.g., insane agility, surprises)
excluded_claims.reason: Videos not reviewed; only titles available, cannot credit capabilities.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: Rainbow Robotics RB-Y1 is a wheeled bimanual mobile manipulator (140 cm tall, 131 kg, two 7-DoF arms, ±0.05 mm repeatability, 20/26 DOF, 1.5 m/s) sold as a research platform for $80,000 (commercial $120,000). It has LiDAR for autonomous movement, force/torque sensors, and supports teleoperation via Master Arm or VR. Evidence includes official specs and pre-order announcement, but no named customer deployments, no autonomous task execution, and all video evidence is title-only without transcript or content review. The robot is purchasable but unproven in real-world use.
strongest_evidence: Official product page with detailed specs and dual-arm whole-body control architecture (rainbow-rb-y1_evidence_001).
Pre-order announcement with pricing and delivery schedule (rainbow-rb-y1_evidence_002).
Media report listing performance videos including water pouring and cup stacking (rainbow-rb-y1_evidence_004).
weakest_evidence: No video transcript or content review; only titles.
No named customers or deployment metrics.
No autonomy demonstration beyond autonomous movement claim.
No runtime or endurance test data.
known_do_not_credit: 24 DOF total (use 20 or 26 from spec table).
Specific capabilities inferred from video titles.
Autonomous task execution (only autonomous movement claimed).
